citations.assessment: The sugya preserves two formulations associated with Rabbi Alexandri, with a competing attribution to Rav Hamnuna for one.
The reciprocal dossier names Alexandri as teacher and points to Midrash HaNe’elam. This is a link to Heilprin’s source trail.
Heilprin’s Pappos dossier preserves the request to see Alexandri’s face in a dream.
Abaye comments on who was excluded. The passage supplies no proof that he and Rabbi Alexandri were contemporaries. The same segment names Alexandri in the burial account.
Rabbi Alexandri transmits Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba. The later report about the end of life also has an alternate attribution.
Rabbi Alexandri transmits the teachings on thunder and the rainbow in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name.
The consulted Yoma reads amar rather than rami and discusses steps after prayer. The rami formula appears in the parallels Heilprin immediately cites from Chelek.
Both reconciliations are brought by Alexandri as contradictions raised by Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.
The successive comments concern the effect of study for its own sake. Alexandri’s first teaching concerns peace in the heavenly and earthly households.
This passage gives the other direction of transmission, with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi reporting in Rabbi Alexandri’s name.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi transmits the reconciliation of the Amalek verses in Rabbi Alexandri’s name.
The text says Rav Mordekhai spoke to him after the teaching about prayer. The recipient is not named anew; Heilprin’s chronology objection remains qualified.
Tanchuma has Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman in Alexandray’s name about Abraham observing eruv tavshilin.
